posts.content: As a good player, favor C when the opponent is likely good; against likely selfish players, D can limit losses. Update beliefs from observed actions and keep prioritizing total good-player payoffs.

Good-role prior gives each other player about 0.291 selfish probability. In each one-off encounter, weigh welfare to all good players: exploit likely selfish opponents, cooperate with likely good ones.
As a good player, favor cooperation: it improves total good-player welfare against good opponents. Against likely selfish opponents, consider defection to protect my own payoff.
Prioritize total welfare of good players; cooperate when the opponent is likely good, and update beliefs from observed actions.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who will defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, favor C against likely good opponents to maximize shared payoff; favor D against likely selfish opponents, since their payoffs are excluded.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Use observed actions and repeat encounters to update beliefs.
As selfish, defect every round: D strictly maximizes payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, who should defect in a one-shot encounter.
For each encounter, favor C when the opponent is likely good; favor D when likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions, but don’t infer P8’s type from P9’s move.
For a good opponent, C maximizes good-player welfare regardless of their action; against a selfish opponent, D improves my payoff. Weigh type uncertainty and update only from actions, not claims.
As a good player, cooperate with good opponents to maximize their combined welfare; defect against selfish opponents to avoid being exploited. Update beliefs from observed play.
As a good player, prioritize total welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
I’ll cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players. P3’s cooperation is weak evidence of being good; update cautiously from observed actions.
Against a likely good opponent, C supports both good players; against a likely selfish opponent, D protects good-player payoffs. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize shared good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed behavior and use the same policy in future encounters.
As selfish, defect every round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize joint good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish opponents, who have an incentive to defect.
Choose C against likely good opponents to maximize joint good-player payoff; choose D against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs only from that opponent’s behavior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when the chance they are selfish exceeds roughly one half. Update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize joint good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who benefit themselves by defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions.

P6 and P7 both cooperated when matched with me, but that alone doesn't establish their roles. Favor C against likely-good players and D when selfishness/defection is likely; weigh the welfare of all good players, not just my payoff.
As a good player, I aim to maximize welfare among good players: cooperate absent evidence of selfishness, and update beliefs from observed actions.
I’m good. C is strictly dominant for selfish players, so observed C identifies good players; cooperate with them, and defect against likely selfish players.
For this round, assess P1 using only reliable encounter evidence; cooperate if likely good and defect if likely selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect every round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish opponents, who benefit from defecting in one-shot encounters. Prior C/C results weakly suggest P3 and P5 are good.
For P10, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish. Use observed behavior as evidence, while remembering selfish players may cooperate strategically.
P4 has no observed record, so retain the role prior. Against an unknown opponent, cooperate when selfish probability is below 1/2; defect above it. Update from actions, not claims.
Against an unknown opponent, cooperate if their selfish probability is below 1/2; otherwise defect. Selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect.
P2’s role is unknown. Cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish players optimally defect and D limits harm. Update beliefs from observed play.
Prioritize welfare of known-good players; defect against strong evidence of selfishness, otherwise cooperate to preserve mutual gains.
Cooperate with known-good opponents; defect against known-selfish opponents. Treat observed C as proof of goodness, but D may come from either type.

Against a good opponent, C maximizes the good players’ combined payoff regardless of their action. Against a selfish opponent, D protects my own included payoff. Use encounter evidence to estimate opponent type.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect.
Continue defecting: D maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s move.
Update beliefs from observed actions; cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. P1 is unobserved, so use the prior.
P9’s defection is strong evidence they’re selfish; cooperation by P8, P7, and P10 supports (but doesn’t prove) they’re good. Against P6, choose to maximize total payoff among good players.
P9 is unobserved; retain the conditional prior (~0.291 selfish). Against a selfish player, D gains 1; against a good player, D sacrifices 1–3 in good-player welfare. Choose by expected welfare.
No evidence about P4 yet. Cooperate with likely-good players to support their welfare; against likely-selfish players, weigh protection from exploitation against harm to any good counterpart.

P7, P6, P5, and P2 cooperated, so they are good under selfish players’ dominant-defection incentives. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents to protect good-player welfare.
Against a selfish opponent, defect to protect good-player payoff; against a good opponent, cooperate to maximize their combined welfare. Use observed behavior to update beliefs.
Selfish players strictly defect. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating C as strong evidence of goodness.

Estimate each opponent’s type from their actual play. Against likely good players, C supports shared good-player payoff; against likely selfish players, D is safer. Past opponents all cooperated, but treat each new pairing independently.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions; selfish players favor D. P10 is untested.
Defect this and every remaining round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Against P8, update suspicion from any known behavior; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish. Preserve cooperation with good players to maximize their combined payoff.
Observed cooperation strongly identifies P6–P8 and P10 as good, while P9’s defection identifies them as selfish. Cooperate with likely-good P2; defect against confirmed selfish opponents.

P1 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not. P9's defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness. Update from actions, not unverifiable claims.
P6, P10, P2, P7, and P4 have cooperated, strong evidence they are good. Against P9, cooperate if selfish probability is below 1/2; otherwise defect.
All five observed opponents chose C, so treat them as good; against P10, choose based on the chance they are selfish: C with a good opponent, D with a selfish one.

P9’s defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; the C encounters are weak evidence of goodness. Cooperate with P8 unless there is specific reason to suspect selfishness, since mutual cooperation benefits good players.

The five opponents who chose C are confirmed good: selfish players strictly prefer D. For P7, use the prior conditioned on those observations; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness likely enough to justify defecting.
P1–P5 all cooperated, so P6 is among the remaining players and may be selfish. Favor D against a likely selfish opponent; C if evidence suggests P6 is good.
Treat P9’s D as evidence of selfishness; the observed Cs support good types. P5 is untested, so choose based on the prior and expected good-player welfare, not certainty.
Defect this round: D yields at least as much as C against either opponent action.

Observed P9 defect against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; P3, P5, P1, P8 cooperated, evidence they’re good. For P4, cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness; preserving C/C yields 6 good-player payoff versus 0 if I defect against good.
P5 is unobserved, so favor C: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ joint payoff. Against a likely selfish opponent, D limits my loss.

Against good players, C maximizes combined good-player welfare; against selfish players, D protects my payoff. Use observed actions as evidence of type, but retain uncertainty. P9's defection is strong selfish evidence; prior cooperators are likely good.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize their combined welfare; against likely-selfish opponents, weigh the harm of mutual defection against exploitation. Update beliefs from observed actions.
The six opponents who chose C are almost certainly good. P9 is untested; defect if selfishness seems more likely than goodness, otherwise cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.
Against P1, cooperate absent evidence they are selfish; defect if credible behavioral evidence indicates selfishness.

The six observed cooperators are good. Given the prior and those observations, two of P2, P9, and P10 are likely selfish. Cooperate with good opponents; against a selfish defector, defect to avoid a payoff of zero.
Six opponents cooperated, so they’re good; selfish players strictly defect. Against P10, cooperate if good seems more likely; defect if selfishness seems more likely.
P9 and P5 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. Prior C behavior supports cooperation. P3 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
Defect this round: D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
With no evidence about P7, favor cooperation; update beliefs from observed behavior and prioritize payoffs to good players.
P9’s defection strongly suggests selfishness; the others I met cooperated. P3 is unobserved, so favor C unless evidence indicates selfishness.
P5 is unobserved. Use the conditional role prior, accounting for evidence from past actions; choose the action with greatest expected cumulative payoff among good players.
Cooperate with P1 unless strong evidence suggests they are selfish; mutual cooperation between good players maximizes their combined welfare.
P9’s defection raises suspicion but is not conclusive. P8 is untested; update from observed actions and choose to maximize expected welfare of all good players.
For P2, weigh the prior chance of selfishness against mutual cooperation’s welfare; defect if selfishness seems more likely than the one-third cutoff, otherwise cooperate.
Observed C proves goodness. The sole selfish player must be P9 or P10, equally likely; against P10, C and D have equal expected good-player payoff.
P1–P6 and P10 cooperated, so they are good. Update remaining-type beliefs among P8/P9; cooperate with P9 if good is more likely, defect if selfishness is more likely.
P4 is untested; cooperate if they seem more likely good than selfish. Use observed actions to refine beliefs, and favor actions that maximize welfare of actual good players.
Defect against P7; as a selfish player, D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

For the remaining encounters, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when selfishness is more likely than goodness. Prior C/C behavior is strong evidence of a good player; P9’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness.
P9’s defection suggests selfishness; P2–P8 and P10 all cooperated when met. P4 is unobserved, so favor C unless evidence indicates otherwise.

P10 is unobserved; use the conditional role prior and action evidence. Against a likely-good player, cooperate to maximize good-player welfare; defect only if selfishness is more likely than goodness.

P5 is unobserved, but all seven other cooperative opponents are good and P9’s defection indicates selfishness. Given the prior and one known selfish player, P5 is good; cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.
Round 9: P1 is the only untested opponent; the seven observed cooperators are likely good, and P9 is suspicious. Choose C if P1 seems good, D if selfish, to maximize good-player welfare.
Round 9: cooperate with P3 unless evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely; defect against a likely selfish player to protect good-player welfare.
All eight observed cooperators are good. Exactly one of P9 and P10 is selfish, equally likely; against P9, C and D have equal expected payoff for the good players.
Against P8, cooperate if they seem likely good; defect if selfishness is more likely. Keep in mind P9’s defection is evidence, not certainty, about their type.
P7 is untested; cooperate if they seem likely good, defect if likely selfish. For good-player welfare, mutual cooperation helps when both are good.
Defect against P6; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P2 is unobserved. Cooperate if they seem more likely good; defect if selfishness is more likely. C/C benefits both good players, while against a selfish defector D improves my own payoff, which counts toward the good-player total.
P5 and I mutually cooperated in round 7, so I expect them to be good; continue prioritizing the combined payoff of good players.
P7 previously reciprocated C, so evidence favors a good role. Cooperate to maximize welfare among good players; update role beliefs from actions, not claims.
P6 cooperated with me in round 1, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate again to maximize good-player welfare.
P10 cooperated against me in round 6, strongly indicating they are good under selfish players’ incentives to defect. For the final encounter, favor C to maximize good-player welfare.
P1 cooperated in our earlier encounter, so cooperate in the final round absent new evidence.
P3 cooperated in our earlier encounter, strongly indicating good; cooperate with P3 to support good-player payoffs.
P2 cooperated previously, identifying them as good under selfish players’ dominant-defection incentives. Cooperate again to maximize shared good-player payoff.
P9 previously defected against my cooperation, so they are likely selfish; if choosing now, defect against them.
Final round: defect against P8; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Round 10: P4 previously cooperated, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate to maximize the good players’ combined payoff.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when the expected total payoff to good players is higher; defect against opponents likely to be selfish. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent to preserve welfare if they are good; update beliefs from encounter outcomes and choose actions to maximize the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when doing so supports good-player welfare; adapt to encounter evidence and defect when it better protects good-player payoffs against selfish play.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since cooperation raises good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, choose actions that maximize expected shared welfare; update beliefs from encounter outcomes.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and account for selfish players’ incentives.
As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when selfishness is more likely. Update beliefs from encounter behavior.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions and results.
Defect every round; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, who should defect in a one-shot encounter.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players overall. Treat P9’s defection as evidence about the selfish count, but not as direct evidence about P8.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; adapt to observed play and defect when that better protects good-player payoffs against selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; observed cooperation identifies P7 as good. Defect against likely-selfish opponents when that better protects good players.
As a good player, cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to increase good players’ combined payoff; defect when selfishness seems sufficiently likely. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect each round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the gain from defecting against a selfish opponent; otherwise defect.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to raise their combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update identity beliefs from that opponent’s observed play.
Cooperate with P3: the observed cooperation by P7 and P8 supports that they are good, and P3 is still more likely good than selfish. Choose actions to maximize total payoff of good players.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; update beliefs from observed play and defect when that better protects good-player payoffs against selfish opponents.
Cooperate with P5, who is more likely good; cooperation benefits both good players. Defect against likely-selfish opponents when that better protects good-player welfare.
Cooperate when expected welfare among good players is higher; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Observed cooperation identifies good players if selfish players optimize their own payoff.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to support their payoff as well as mine; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good than selfish; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect every round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish opponents. Prior C/C results indicate P3 and P5 are good.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. P10 has no observed behavior, so use the prior belief.
Cooperate with unknown P4: the prior chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good-player welfare; adapt to observed actions and defect when likely selfish play makes that better for the good players.
Cooperate with P2, who is more likely good; cooperation maximizes combined good-player welfare against a good opponent. P5, P6, and P7 are good given their observed cooperation.
Cooperate with likely good players to preserve shared welfare; defect when strong evidence indicates a selfish opponent.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize the good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Observed cooperation is strong evidence of a good player.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to raise good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with unobserved P1; C is best when they are more likely good than selfish. Prior C/C actions make P3 and P5 likely good; P9's defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation raises good players’ combined payoff. Update beliefs from each opponent’s observed action.
Cooperate with unobserved P9: the conditional selfish probability is below the welfare-based threshold. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents when that improves expected welfare.
Cooperate with P3: good-player welfare favors C against a good opponent, and my selfishness estimate is below the threshold for D. Continue updating beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate to maximize shared welfare with a likely good opponent; defect only when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player payoffs; selfish players strictly defect, so observed cooperation identifies good players.

Cooperate with P5: the observed cooperation by P1–P4 indicates they are good; among the remaining players selfishness is still less likely than goodness. Update beliefs from reliable encounter actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents when expected good-player welfare favors it; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. P9's defection raises my estimate of their selfishness.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Prior C/C evidence makes P3 and P5 likely good; P9’s D raises suspicion.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize the total payoff of good players; defect against likely selfish opponents. P2 has no observed behavior, so use the prior adjusted for P9’s defection.

Cooperate with unknown P1: their selfish-role probability remains below the welfare threshold. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and P9's defection as strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents when it protects good players' payoffs.
Cooperate: against a good opponent, C increases combined good-player welfare whether they choose C or D. The expected benefit outweighs the loss from an opponent who is selfish and defects.
Defect when the chance of facing a selfish opponent outweighs the welfare gained from mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed behavior.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect only when selfishness is more likely than goodness. Observed cooperation identifies good players under selfish players’ incentives.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared good-player payoffs; defect when selfishness is more likely. P1–P5 cooperated, so update beliefs among the remaining players.
Cooperate with P5: untested opponents are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation benefits good-player welfare. Observed C actions lower estimates; P9’s D raises theirs.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with P4, who is more likely good than selfish; C/C maximizes combined good-player payoffs. Update identity beliefs from observed cooperation and defection.

Cooperate with P5 unless they are more likely selfish; mutual cooperation yields the best combined payoff for good players. Observed cooperation identifies good players, while P9’s defection raises their selfishness likelihood.

Cooperate with P6: the cooperative records make several players likely good, while P9's defection is strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. Choose to maximize total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.

Cooperate with untested P9: the posterior selfishness chance is about one-third, below the threshold where defecting better protects good-player welfare. Prior cooperation identifies P2, P3, P5, P6, P7, and P10 as good.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent unless evidence makes selfishness likely enough to outweigh mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize combined good-player payoffs; defect if an opponent is likely selfish. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play.
Observed cooperation identifies P1–P6 as good. Among P8–P10, selfishness remains below half, so cooperate with P10 to maximize expected good-player payoff.
Cooperate with untested opponents when likely good; mutual cooperation improves good-player welfare. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness.
As selfish, defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with unobserved P7: C/C yields more total payoff if they are good, and the chance of gaining by defecting against a selfish opponent is not enough to offset that.
Cooperate with P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P3 is very likely good based on the observed cooperation pattern.

Cooperate with P5: the prior and observed cooperation records make them likely good. Treat P9's defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness; choose actions to maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat P9's defection as strong evidence, while cooperative opponents are likely good.
Cooperate with untested P8: the six observed cooperators are likely good, while P9’s defection raises suspicion. Choose C when P8 is more likely good to maximize expected welfare of all good players.
Cooperate with P2 absent behavioral evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions and protect good-player welfare when selfishness is likely.

The seven observed cooperators are good. Given the prior and those observations, P9 and P10 are equally likely to be the sole selfish player; C and D have equal expected good-player payoff against P10, so I choose C.
Cooperate with likely-good P9 to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs cautiously from observed play.

Cooperate with untested P4: their observed type is more likely good, and cooperation benefits good-player welfare against a cooperative good opponent. Treat P5 and P9’s defections as evidence of selfishness.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with P6 absent strong evidence of selfishness; C/C benefits good players. Prior C actions strongly indicate good roles, while P9’s D against my C raises suspicion.
Cooperate with P4; observed play indicates P4 is good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with unobserved P10: their selfishness probability is below the welfare-based threshold. P9's defection strongly suggests selfishness; prior cooperators are likely good.

Cooperate with P5 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. P9's defection is strong evidence of selfishness, while prior count constraints leave P5 as the main alternative.

Cooperate with P1 unless selfishness is sufficiently likely; C benefits both good players more than D harms them. Prior cooperation strongly identifies the other observed players as good; P9’s defection raises suspicion.
Cooperate with P3 absent strong evidence of selfishness; preserve mutual welfare and update beliefs from observed behavior.
The eight observed cooperators are good; P9 and P10 are equally likely to be the sole selfish player. C and D have equal expected good-player payoff against P9, so I choose C.
Cooperate with P8 to maximize the combined payoff of good players.
Cooperate with untested P7: their selfishness is uncertain, and cooperation supports welfare if they are good. Prior defections from P5 and P9 make them more likely selfish.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against P2 because the remaining selfish-player count and P9’s defection make P2’s selfishness plausible enough to outweigh the benefit of C/C.
Cooperate with P5: their earlier cooperation strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes the good players’ combined payoff.
Cooperate with P7, whose prior cooperation strongly suggests they are good. Defections by P9 and P10 are evidence of selfishness; cooperate to maximize welfare among good players.
Cooperate with P6: our prior mutual cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes their combined welfare.

Cooperate choices identify the other observed players as good; given the required selfish-player counts, P9 is the remaining possible selfish player. Defect to protect good-player welfare in the final round.
Cooperate with P1, whose earlier cooperation indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes welfare between good players.
P3’s earlier cooperation identifies them as good. Cooperating supports both good players’ payoffs against them.
P2 previously cooperated, indicating they are good. Cooperate to maximize the combined payoff of good players.
Cooperate on the final encounter: P9’s defection leaves them uncertain, and cooperation favors good-player welfare if they are good.
Defect in the final round; D maximizes my payoff against either action.
Cooperate with P4: their earlier cooperation identifies them as good, and C/C gives the good players more total payoff than D/C.
Cooperated in every encounter, prioritizing good players’ combined payoff; inferred P9 was selfish from their defection and the others good from their cooperation.
As a good player, I cooperated to support good-player welfare and used observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness, while treating cooperative responses as evidence of good roles.
Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; the cooperating opponents are good, and the count prior makes P9 the remaining selfish player.
Cooperated throughout to maximize good-player welfare; inferred cooperators were good and P9 was the remaining possible selfish player, so defected against P10 in the final round.
Cooperated with players who showed no evidence of selfishness and defected once against a likely selfish opponent, aiming to maximize welfare among good players.
Cooperated with observed cooperators, since selfish players strictly prefer defection. P9’s defection identifies them as selfish; all other players are good.
Cooperated to maximize shared payoffs against likely good players; the sole observed defection came from P9, while every other opponent cooperated.
Cooperated throughout to support welfare among good players. Treated P5 and especially P9’s defections as evidence of selfishness, while updating from cooperative actions.
Defected every round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperated with players who had previously cooperated; defected when selfishness seemed sufficiently likely.

P1.strategy: Cooperated in every encounter, prioritizing good players’ combined payoff; inferred P9 was selfish from their defection and the others good from their cooperation.

P2.strategy: As a good player, I cooperated to support good-player welfare and used observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness, while treating cooperative responses as evidence of good roles.

P3.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare; the cooperating opponents are good, and the count prior makes P9 the remaining selfish player.

P4.strategy: Cooperated throughout to maximize good-player welfare; inferred cooperators were good and P9 was the remaining possible selfish player, so defected against P10 in the final round.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with players who showed no evidence of selfishness and defected once against a likely selfish opponent, aiming to maximize welfare among good players.

P6.strategy: Cooperated with observed cooperators, since selfish players strictly prefer defection. P9’s defection identifies them as selfish; all other players are good.

P7.strategy: Cooperated to maximize shared payoffs against likely good players; the sole observed defection came from P9, while every other opponent cooperated.

P8.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support welfare among good players. Treated P5 and especially P9’s defections as evidence of selfishness, while updating from cooperative actions.

P9.strategy: Defected every round; D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with players who had previously cooperated; defected when selfishness seemed sufficiently likely.
